Prior to declaring weighed-in the Stewards considered an application from Jockey M Chadwick that his horse be declared a non-runner on the basis that it had been denied a fair start.  After taking evidence from Starter Mr A Speechley, Jockey Chadwick and Trainer C H Yip, the Stewards found that as the start was being effected SMART HIGH reared and as a consequence lost significant ground.  As the Stewards were satisfied that the Starter could not have reasonably anticipated the horse was going to rear it was declared a runner.  Before being allowed to race again, SMART HIGH will be required to perform satisfactorily in a barrier trial.

Bumped shortly after the start.  When questioned regarding his riding in the Home Straight Z Purton stated that his mount was able to show good pace in the early stages to lead the event.  He said after entering the Home Straight his mount naturally improved away from the field and established a break on other runners.  He said as he approached the 200 Metres he was concerned that the horse was commencing to peak on its run and for this reason he held the horse together whilst continuing to encourage it until near the 200 Metres.  He added after passing the 200 Metres he then placed his mount under full pressure where it responded to his riding, however, over the concluding stages was unable to hold off the eventual winner PACKING GLORY.  After considering his explanation the Stewards found the tactics adopted by Jockey Purton were reasonable in the circumstances.  Sent for sampling post-race.

When questioned B Avdulla stated that from an inside barrier he was able to hold a slightly more forward position than its previous race starts.  He said throughout the middle stages he followed PATCH OF THETA and he had LITTLE PARADISE positioned to his outside.  He said whilst he contemplated shifting out from the 600 Metres he felt he was not in a position to do so as LITTLE PARADISE was racing slightly in advance of his mount and travelling well at that stage.  He said as he did not want to follow TOMODACHI KOKOROE he remained racing behind PATCH OF THETA.  He added that on entering the Home Straight when PATCH OF THETA shifted out he took the only option available to shift to the outside of PATCH OF THETA, however, became held up behind COPARTNER PRANCE near the 250 Metres when that runner commenced to give ground.  He further stated that he then looked to shift to the outside of COPARTNER PRANCE leaving the 200 Metres as he was of the opinion that COPARTNER PRANCE may continue to shift in when it was giving ground, however when COPARTNER PRANCE shifted out slightly this resulted in RAGING BLIZZARD being steadied when disappointed for clear running between COPARTNER PRANCE and PATCH OF THETA and as a result RAGING BLIZZARD did not obtain clear running between the 250 Metres and the 50 Metres.

Trainer D A Hayes advised that the horse had pleased him leading into the race and he was satisfied with the position the horse had obtained in the early stages.  He said SHAMUS STORM was disadvantaged by racing too keenly throughout the middle stages which left it without a finishing effort in the Home Straight.  He added that SHAMUS STORM would now be spelled and dropped back in distance.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  Sent for sampling post-race.

C L Chau reported that his mount hung out throughout the event and leaving the 300 Metres shifted out abruptly and as a consequence he could not ride the horse out for the remainder of the event.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The racing manners of JIN SHENG were considered unacceptable.  Before being allowed to race again, JIN SHENG will be required to perform satisfactorily in a barrier trial around a bend. Approaching the 300 Metres was hampered when taken wider by JIN SHENG.  Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  H T Mo stated that when his mount jumped well it raced in a more forward position than instructed.

Jumped awkwardly, shifted out and made contact with ALMIGHTY LIGHTNING.  Sent for sampling post-race.

On jumping was crowded between COOL BOY and GLORIOUS DYNASTY, both of which shifted ground.  Between the 500 Metres and the 350 Metres was held up for clear running. J Orman was advised to exercise more care.  C Y Ho stated that near the 500 Metres he felt his mount was being galloped on when WINNING GOLD shifted to the outside of ALL’S WELL.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

From the 400 Metres became held up behind EVERYONE’S STAR and was shifted to the inside of that runner. As a result MONARCH COUNTY made contact with GALACTIC VOYAGE. Shifted in at the start and was bumped.  Near the 350 Metres was steadied when crowded between GALACTIC VOYAGE and MONARCH COUNTY (J Moreira) which, after improving to the inside of EVERYONE’S STAR, then shifted in further when being checked to avoid SEWARD which was giving ground.  Whilst the Stewards accepted that Jockey Moreria had taken evasive action to avoid SEWARD and then corrected his mount when it shifted in towards GLORIOUS DYNASTY, he was reprimanded and advised in similar circumstances he would be expected to make a greater effort to provide due care to his fellow riders.
